newsitem.title: KENYA: Kenya shares drift despite foreign buying.
newsitem.headline: Kenya shares drift despite foreign buying.

text.p: The Nairobi Stock Exchange (NSE) fell by 0.66 of a point on Tuesday despite renewed interest in financial stocks from foreign investors, traders said.

Trading was slow on the NSE 20-share index which closed at 3419.36, with turnover falling to 19.5 million shillings ($280,000) traded on 457,675 shares from 27.1 million dealt on 541,859 shares on Tuesday.
Dealers said foreign interest was reviving in the financial counters -- traditional focal points for foreign speculators.
"They are buying in small amounts, we get orders for 50,000 rather than a million (shilling's worth of shares)," a bourse floor dealer told Reuters.

Foreign investors have been buying few shares during August because of economic turmoil triggered by violence at political rallies since May and the International Monetary Fund's withholding of a key aid package on July 31 citing corruption.

Bourse officials said the move back into the financial board was cautious, with foreigners buying 112 shares in National Industrial Credit at 51 shillings from 50 and 3,000 Kenya Commercial Bank shares at between 97-98.5 shillings from 98.
On the special board foreign investors moved over a quarter of Tuesday's turnover, buying 200,000 Firestone East Africa shares at 28 shillings unchanged.
Foreigners purchased a further 27,000 shares in Kenya Power and Lighting at 160 shillings unchanged.
Outside the foreign board, two counters were active in the agricultural sector, with Rea Vipingo trading 6,600 shares at between 8.10-8.65 shillings from 8.5.
Brooke Bond traded 1,195 shares at between 123 and 124 shillings from 123.
Lonrho Motors continued sliding downwards to close at 47.75 shillings from 49.75. Kenya Airways moved 42,340 shares at prices hovering between 8-8.1 shillings.
The industrial sector took up 67 percent of Tuesday's volume with recent arrival Athi River Mining trading 53,100 shares at between 11.95-12.5 shillings from 12.25.
Turnover of the fourth issue of the Central Bank of Kenya floating-rate treasury bond remained high at 350.3 million shillings, although lower than Monday's record 498.5 million.
The bonds changed hands at 103.0000 percent from 102.9800 percent.
